Extremely fun and challenging game! One of the coolest "town-building" games I've played. Having to prepare the town before you get wiped by a blizzard, upgrade everything with little resources, and maintain civility is a hell of a game. The importance to learn the strategy of the game early did not hit me til I failed like 3 times. The beginning starts off pretty quickly which makes the challenge. Every decision makes a impact. It consistently makes you think on your feet, and be 3 moves ahead of yourself at all times. Scenarios that can end the game part-way through, making you adapt your playstyle not like boring idle town games. Picture: After a rocky start, you finally get everything under control, then next thing you know its so cold your'e destroying everything that's not a house to burn for heat. *10/10

Also words can't describe how incredible the art and the music is in this game.

This game is insane. Got it on sale and it's a bargain.

The gameplay mixes hope, fear, and brutal moral choices. As a player, you constantly feel the pressure to keep your colony alive. Resource management, careful building placement, and thinking ahead are key to success. As I was playing, I was so immersed I lost track of time. The music, combined with the sad fate of the citizens, gives you a wistful yet powerful feeling to try and achieve the best possible outcome.

10/10, a masterpiece.

Frostpunk is a brutal, yet incredibly immersive city-builder where every decision feels heavy. Balancing the survival of your people with tough moral choices is both stressful and rewarding. The cold, the limited resources, and the constant need to make hard calls kept me on edge the whole time. It's not just about building a city; it's about keeping hope alive. If you enjoy a challenge and don't mind a bit of heartbreak, this game is a must-play.

i bought this game when it was full price and i would buy it again at full price right now even having played it through to its entirety. I really enjoyed every aspect of this game from the art work to the story mode game play to the different challenges that come up. There is a lot of upgrade and different game play styles to play around with. I have been waiting for Frostpunk 2 with much excitement. I have nothing but great things to say about this game and the devs that created it. Congrats on a successful game, i cant wait for the next one!

I dabble in city management games occasionally, but this is the first one that I've stuck with throughout a full campaign. For starters, you can finish the initial scenario in about ten hours, so it doesn't outstay its welcome. That campaign is well paced so you always feel like you're making progress, but struggling. It presents you with some interesting ethical choices: whether to force children to work, provide palliative care for the gravely ill, lead with an even hand or set yourself up as a religious despot, etc. I also liked that there was no warfare to deal with; I always find it tedious when that's slapped onto a city management game, as in some of the later Settlers titles. Also, its central concept of coping with the temperature as much as resource management gave it an interesting spin. It was a weird experience playing this during the hottest week of the year so far; I was trying to stop my citizens freezing in Frostpunk while trying to stop myself roasting in real life.

A good game, surprisingly engaging. Every circumstance is a balancing act. Understanding how to walk the line between the necessities of survival and tyranny causes a lot of moral quandary. Although it's very intensive on the processing power; for a game about the deadly cold I hadn't expected it to heat up my computer (a few years out of date, admitted) so much. Still, if your heatsinks and fans are strong enough for it, a damn good game with a lot of interesting challenges.

Absolutely a great game you have to play. Played it and all the xpacs, great base builder. The xpacs don't add too much, but they are absolutely fun and worth getting. One of the few games I paid full price for and never regretted it.

...Well, maybe regretted the few times staying up late thinking I could handle a tougher difficulty as everything spiraled out of control and I both lost the game and lost hours of sleep.

Frostpunk became very quickly one of my favorite games. I particularly liked the storyline, which most city-builder/resource management games don't really have. I found myself feeling sorry for my citizens and struggled to make the right choices. That emotional element added a lot to the gameplay and after my first play-through, I immediately wanted to try and get a "better ending." If you like a resource management game that's a little more on the brutal and difficult side, I highly recommend this one. You can absolutely mess everything up from the first 5 minutes, which I personally find very enjoyable, but I have a masochistic streak.

Some of the DLC is pretty hit-or-miss. The base game alone is very fun, and the Fall of Winterholme is quite challenging (I found the first scenario pretty easy). For DLC, I think the "Last Autumn" is pretty fun but found the last expansion, "On the Edge" to be very disappointing and honestly a little anti-climatic. It was so easy that I thought I might have put it on the wrong setting. I basically played through it and got a bunch of achievements when I hadn't played the game in over a year--definitely too easy for Frostpunk.

Hands down one of the best games I have ever played. Holy crap. 

I don't even know what I could say that hasn't been said but this game really makes you weigh your decisions and consider and reconsider. Your decisions have weight and even small things can have big consequences that you will have to accept and adapt to. 

The art direction, sound track, worldbuilding, writing, design, etc. is all extremely good. Some of the character dialog feels like a punch in the gut. 

This game is pure art in its highest form. I see myself putting a lot more time into this one.

Frostpunk could potentially be a great building/strategy game. Unfortunately, it is bogged down by linear scenarios with no random elements to them. The same things happen at the same time, in the same order. You only need to learn and prepare in advance. This kills replay value.

Only 4 scenarios are available to play and then the game wants you to buy DLCs for more. There is a steep learning curve to the first scenario (A new Home), but thanks to the lessons learned, the 3 others become easy and can be cleared on the first attempt.

This game needed a default sandbox mode with a random starting location, random events and random map (outside your city)

THE CITY MUST SURVIVE.

No but for real, I never thought a city management strategy game would made me cry but here we are. The dread of the calendar ticking down each day until disaster, desperately trying to scrounge together enough food and coal to survive, only to have half my population perish all the same, while the desperation of my people is reflected perfectly in the soundtrack, watching the city I'd worked so hard to build, freeze over and die, clinging on to dear life.

My favourite part of the game is the sound design, the atmosphere of the city (which changes based on your actions) is represented more than anything through sound, your actions are felt more than anything through screaming guards or chanting priests. The soundtrack is extraordinary, too. It's not a game for everybody, but if you have the patience to see it through, it's absolutely captivating.

Frostpunk is in a strange niche of a genre, being a resource-management city-building game, but if you can learn its mechanics, its well worth the effort. It's a story of fear, desperation, and the triumph of the human spirit and perseverance in the face of inevitable collapse. The city must survive.

Rich storylines and hard moral problems make Frostpunk unique among city building games. Citizens feel more like a responsibility than a statistic thanks to a running narrative and meaningful consequences to the decisions you make.

The biggest tragedy is that the game does not have more scenarios or a way to mod in scenarios.

This is the first city builder that I have genuinely enjoyed playing, and will play more of.
I find most city builders to be boring time-wasters that at best, are games of automation and monitoring, and at worst err on glorifying colonialism.

Frost Punk, in its post-apocalyptic setting, asks us to imagine and simulate the future we want to see, or that we dare to be curious about. This particular edition is set in an outpost by refugees from London who must survive in frozen wasteland and rebuild society.

While other city builders demand that you operate society like a switchboard, Frost Punk asks you to engage your conscience into strategic decisions. If food is low and sick workers are plenty, do you make soup so that everyone stays fed, or do you add sawdust to the rations for the illusion of prosperity? Are children to be shielded from labour in safehouses, or made to grow up too soon? Will you use the church or state to motivate and influence the community, or will you rely on solidarity alone?

The choice, resources permitting, is usually yours.

A solid 7/10. I would buy it on sale as the price is steep-ish for what it is.

IMHO there is a misconception among certain group of players.
While Frostpunk involves building a city and managing resources, it isn't meant to be a city builder game.
Thus, if you expect it to be a city builder, it probably wouldn't match your expectation and you will be disappointed.

Frostpunk is more like an interactive story with the skin of a city builder - just like This War of Mine, which is also an interactive story told through a surival game. So, if you want to experience stories of people struggling under very harsh circumstances with challenging resource management gameplay (and great soundtrack), this game is for you.

That said, Frostpunk has some core city builder elements (that's why people have such misconception) and endless city building mode is under great demand. The devs will probably implement an endless mode really soon. While I am AGAINST such mode as this kind of taking away a core element of the game (the story/journey), but I would still be giving it a try when such mode is implemented as I really like the works of the devs.

TL;DR
Frostpunk is NOT a city builder. It is an experience of of people struggling told through a game of resource management.
